evidence.quote: The cast polycrystalline alloy was prepared from the appropriate amounts of elemental metals by arc melting in Ar. The mass of Al was increased by a factor of 1.05 and added in the ﬁnal melting stage to compensate for the loss of Al due to the evaporation during the melting process. The alloy was inverted and melted more than eight times to attain a homogeneous composition.
Homogenization heat treatment was conducted at 1250°C for 12 h, followed by air cooling to reduce the segregation of as-cast alloy.

mechanisms.name: Cr partition to γ decreasing interfacial energy

evidence.quote: the “rate-limiting element Cr” in alloy 9CoNi-Cr is strongly partitioned into the γ phase, and the concentration gradient across the γ/γ′ interface is large, which has the advantage of decreasing the interfacial energy of the alloy
which can be attributed to the formation of a continuous Al2O3 protective layer

Moreover, Cr is also an important γ strengthening element [52], and its strong partition to the γ phase improves the strength of the γ matrix. Thus, the high Cr content is probably the reason for the high overall strength of alloy 9CoNi-Cr.

a novel CoNi-based superalloy with superior comprehensive performance, alloy 9CoNi-Cr, was developed.
This alloy retained a high volume fraction, stable morphology, and slow coarsening of γ′ precipitates during the long-term aging at 900–1000°C.
A continuous Al2O3 layer could form during 1000°C oxidation, and the oxidation resistance is superior to conventional Ni-based cast superalloy MarM247.
Thus, the high Cr content is probably the reason for the high overall strength of alloy 9CoNi-Cr.
